actually_read: Definition 27, Theorem 28 and Proposition 29, printed p.2025
source_reading.exact_quote: For these models causal minimality reduces to the condition that each function fj is not constant in any of its arguments:
source_reading.formal_quantifier: for all j and i ∈ PAj there are some x_PA_j_without_i and some xi != xi_prime such that fj(x_other,xi) != fj(x_other,xi_prime)
source_reading.proof_justification: Parent-noise independence gives conditional translated densities; equality of two translates implies equal shifts since a probability law has no nonzero period. Positivity upgrades conditional almost-everywhere to Lebesgue almost-everywhere, and continuity extends constancy to all parent inputs. Positive-density intersection then preserves dependence for every intermediate nondescendant conditioning set. This is the local authored proof, avoiding the source A.4 unnecessary finite-mean simplification.

counterexample.construction: Independent standard normals H,N_X,N_Z,N_Y; X=H+N_X, Z=H+N_Z, Y=X+N_Y. DAG1 has H→X,H→Z,X→Y; DAG2 adds Z→Y with f_Y(x,z)=x. Both give the same positive observational density; all nonroot functions are aggregate-nonconstant, but Z is an inessential parent.
counterexample.consequence: Refutes aggregate nonconstancy as a definition sufficient for parent-dependence and conditioned-reversal.
counterexample.limit: The second model is not restricted: for edge Z→Y the structural slice is constant, so f_prime=0 and no Condition19 witness exists. This example must not be described as a counterexample to the full restricted-ANM theorem.
